purpose: This medication is a birth control pill used to prevent pregnancy. It may also be prescribed to help regulate menstrual cycles or reduce menstrual cramps. Some forms are used to treat acne in women who also need contraception.
how_it_works: This pill contains two hormones, estrogen and progestin, that work together to prevent pregnancy in a few ways. They stop your ovaries from releasing an egg each month. They also thicken the mucus in your cervix so sperm have a harder time getting through, and they thin the lining of the uterus.
common_side_effects: Nausea, headaches, breast tenderness or swelling, spotting or light bleeding between periods especially in the first few months, mood changes, decreased sex drive, and bloating. These often improve after the first 2 to 3 months.
warnings: Do not smoke while taking this pill, especially if you are over 35, as it greatly increases your risk of serious blood clots, stroke, or heart attack. Tell your doctor if you have a history of blood clots, high blood pressure, migraines with aura, liver problems, or breast cancer. This pill does NOT protect against sexually transmitted infections.
typical_dosing: Take one pill by mouth every day at the same time each day. This pack contains 28 pills with different colored pills for different phases of your cycle, including some reminder pills that contain no hormones. Start your next pack the day after you finish your current one with no break in between.
